In [[mathematics]], [[George Glauberman]]'s '''ZJ theorem''' states that if a [[finite group]] ''G'' is ''p''-constrained and [[p-stable group|''p''-stable]] and has a [[normal subgroup|normal]] [[p-group|''p''-subgroup]] for some [[parity (mathematics)|odd]] [[prime number|prime]] ''p'', then ''O''<sub>''{{prime|p}}''</sub>(''G'')''Z''(''J''(''S'')) is a normal [[subgroup]] of ''G'', for any [[Sylow subgroup|Sylow ''p''-subgroup]] ''S''.

==Notation and definitions==
*''J''(''S'') is the '''[[Thompson subgroup]]''' of a ''p''-group ''S'': the subgroup generated by the [[abelian group|abelian subgroups]] of maximal [[order (group theory)|order]].
*''Z''(''H'') means the [[center (group theory)|center]] of a group ''H''.
*''O''<sub>''{{prime|p}}''</sub> is the maximal normal subgroup of ''G'' of order [[coprime]] to ''p'', the [[Core (group theory)#The_p-core|''{{prime|p}}''-core]]
*''O''<sub>''p''</sub> is the maximal normal ''p''-subgroup of ''G'', the [[p-core|''p''-core]].
*''O''<sub>''{{prime|p}}'',''p''</sub>(''G'') is the maximal normal [[p-nilpotent group|''p''-nilpotent subgroup]] of ''G'', the [[Core (group theory)#The_p-core|''{{prime|p}}'',''p''-core]], part of the [[upper p-series|upper ''p''-series]].
*For an odd prime ''p'', a group ''G'' with ''O''<sub>''p''</sub>(''G'') ≠ 1 is said to be '''[[p-stable group|''p''-stable]]''' if whenever ''P'' is a {{nowrap|''p''-subgroup}} of ''G'' such that ''PO<sub>{{prime|p}}</sub>''(''G'') is normal in ''G'', and [''P'',''x'',''x''] = 1, then the image of ''x'' in N<sub>''G''</sub>(''P'')/C<sub>''G''</sub>(''P'') is contained in a normal {{nowrap|''p''-subgroup}} of N<sub>''G''</sub>(''P'')/C<sub>''G''</sub>(''P'').
*For an odd prime ''p'', a group ''G'' with ''O''<sub>''p''</sub>(''G'') ≠ 1 is said to be '''[[p-constrained group|''p''-constrained]]''' if the [[centralizer]] C<sub>''G''</sub>(''P'') is contained in ''O''<sub>''{{prime|p}}'',''p''</sub>(''G'') whenever ''P'' is a Sylow {{nowrap|''p''-subgroup}} of ''O''<sub>''{{prime|p}}'',''p''</sub>(''G'').
